Window drawn by the system. Works with debugging off. Note: while it is on screen, your keyboard closes whenever the agent touches it or opens a new screen in it, which makes typing hard. Tap the close button (square with an X) to close it.
Does not disturb your keyboard. Can be hidden, resized, made translucent and used. Turns debugging on only while the window is open, and closes if the phone screen turns off.

The token field is always reported as a password to the agent, even when shown.
Every action is recorded in an append-only audit log on your computer.
The small red button on screen cancels the agent\'s current action; the agent is told and nothing needs re-enabling. To fully disconnect, use the notification or this app.
Ask before using the main screen
If you are using the phone, the agent asks before tapping or typing on your screen. Background windows never ask.
Acts on your screen without asking
Let the agent use your screen?
You are using the phone. The agent wants to tap and type on the main screen. The red button cancels it anytime.
Dangerous: full access to your phone

With this on, the agent can unlock your phone by itself and reach everything on it: banking, email, messages, passwords and verification codes. Anyone who controls the agent, your computer or the relay gets the same power. Use only if you understand and accept the risk.
Uses the saved PIN on the lock screen. One wrong attempt turns this off automatically.

The DroidHand authors and contributors are not liable. The PIN stays encrypted on this phone (Android Keystore) and is never sent to the agent or the relay.

Read-only. Phones and their settings are configured on the computer (devices.json).
Each phone has its own token. You set it up on the computer that runs the relay, then on the new phone. About 10 minutes. Tap a command to copy it.
Create a token for the new phone. Replace <id> with a short name (lowercase letters, digits, - or _), e.g. tablet.
Add the phone to ~/.config/droidhand/devices.json, inside \"devices\" (put a comma after the previous entry):
\"role\": \"admin\" lets the phone open this Relay screen. For a test phone whose ADB is always on, add \"adb\": { \"mode\": \"always\", \"serial\": \"<ip>:5555\" }.
Restart the relay so it reads the new phone:
Install Tailscale and sign in to the same tailnet as the computer.
Install DroidHand from the latest release (the .apk file) and open it.
Under Connection, enter the same relay address this phone uses: %1$s, and paste the new phone\'s token. The computer prints it with:

In the Permissions panel, turn on Accessibility (if it is greyed out: App info → ⋮ → Allow restricted settings), Notifications and Unrestricted battery. On Samsung also: Battery → Background usage limits → Never sleeping apps → DroidHand.
Once, from the computer: turn on Wireless debugging on the new phone, pair it (Pair device with pairing code, then adb pair <ip:port> on the computer), connect and run:
Then turn debugging off again: from now on the agent turns ADB on and off by itself when a task needs it.
With the new phone already connected over adb, this does steps 5, 6, the accessibility switch and step 8 in one go (run it in the droidhand folder; Tailscale and battery are still up to you):
The new phone shows up as connected in the Relay list. Agents pick a phone with device=\"<id>\" (list_devices shows them all).
Full guide: docs/setup.md, section \"Several phones\", in the project repository.
